entities.summary:
Boncompagno da Signa was a prominent Italian scholar, grammarian, historian, and philosopher of the 13th century. Born in Pavia, Italy, he was a key figure in the development of the University of Bologna, where he taught and contributed to the field of grammar and rhetoric. His most notable work, the 'Liber de distinctione verborum' ('Treatise on the Distinction of Words'), became a standard reference for grammar and language learning in the Middle Ages.

 Da Signa's writings also touched on the subjects of history, philosophy, and the interpretation of ancient texts. His works often critiqued the prevailing intellectual trends of his time, advocating for a more nuanced understanding of language and its relationship to human culture. Through his scholarship, Da Signa played a significant role in shaping the intellectual landscape of medieval Italy, influencing generations of scholars and thinkers to come.

 In the centuries following his death in 1250, Da Signa's works continued to be studied and admired for their intellectual rigor and cultural significance. Today, he remains a notable figure in the history of Italian scholarship, remembered for his commitment to the advancement of language, history, and philosophy in the medieval world.

 'A true scholar of the human tongue is also a scholar of the human condition.'— Boncompagno da Signa
